note: What people score on the same tests. Hand-collected, one entry per published figure, each with the sentence that states it. A benchmark with no entry here has no human baseline published - which is most of them.

entries.who: PhD holders and candidates answering questions in their own field
entries.quote: experts who have or are pursuing PhDs in the corresponding domains reach 65% accuracy (74% when discounting clear mistakes the experts identified in retrospect)

entries.who: skilled non-experts with over 30 minutes and unrestricted web access
entries.quote: highly skilled non-expert validators only reach 34% accuracy, despite spending on average over 30 minutes with unrestricted access to the web

entries.who: estimated expert level, from 95th-percentile scores on the real exams the questions come from
entries.quote: If we take the 95th percentile human test-taker accuracy for exams that build up our test, and if we make an educated guess when such information is unavailable, we then estimate that expert-level accuracy is approximately 89.8%

entries.who: a three-time IMO gold medallist, on a 20-problem sample
entries.quote: A three-time IMO gold medalist got 18/20 = 90%, though missed questions were exclusively due to small errors of arithmetic.

entries.who: a computer-science PhD student who does not especially like maths
entries.quote: a computer science PhD student who does not especially like mathematics attained approximately 40% on MATH, while a three-time IMO gold medalist attained 90%

entries.who: human performance on the testmini split, as reported by the authors
entries.quote: GPT-4V ... achieves 49.9% accuracy, which is only 58% of human performance at 60.3%

entries.who: human experts, best of three panels (medium 82.6, low 76.2)
entries.quote: Human Expert (High), validation overall 88.6 - published on the MMMU leaderboard, 2024-01-31

entries.who: a panel of over 400 members of the public - the figure is task coverage, not one person's accuracy
entries.quote: 100% of tasks have been solved by at least 2 humans (many by more) in under 2 attempts.
